{{more footnotes|date=October 2011}}
'''Stefan Jentsch''' (29 May 1955 – 29 October 2016) was a German [[cell biologist]]. He was a director at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in Martinsried, Germany. He is known for his pioneering work in the field of protein modifications by [[ubiquitin]] and ubiquitin-like modifiers.

== Life ==
Jentsch was born in [[Berlin]] and studied [[biology]] at the [[Free University of Berlin]], where he also obtained his [[Diplom]] in 1979. He then completed his Ph.D. at the [[Max Planck Institute for Molecular Genetics]] in Berlin in 1983.

After his Ph.D., he joined the laboratory of [[Alexander Varshavsky]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. In 1988 he returned to Germany, becoming a junior group leader at the [[Friedrich Miescher]] Laboratory of the [[Max Planck Society]] in [[Tübingen]] in 1988 and then professor at the Center of Molecular Biology (ZMBH), [[University of Heidelberg]] in 1993. From 1998 until his death he was a director of the Department of Molecular Cell Biology, the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in Martinsried. Jentsch died in [[Munich]] on 29 October 2016.<ref>[http://www.biochem.mpg.de/5397125/stefan-jentsch-passed-away Stefan Jentsch passed away – Obituary of the MPI of Biochemistry]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=Stefan Jentsch (1955–2016)|volume=167|issue=7|pages=1667–1668|journal=Cell|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2016.11.057|year=2016|last1=Sommer|first1=Thomas|last2=Hoppe|first2=Thorsten|last3=Rape|first3=Michael|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Prizes and awards ==
* 1992 [[Klung Wilhelmy Science Award|Otto Klung Prize for Chemistry]]
* 1993 [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]]
* 1996 [[Otto Bayer Award]]
* 2003 Max-Planck Research Award
* 2006 Honorary Professorship of [[Fudan University]]
* 2011 [[Louis-Jeantet Prize for Medicine]]
* 2017 [[Otto Warburg Medal]]
